method: Split conformal prediction on spatial (leave-districts-out) out-of-fold errors of the share model, 4 bins by predicted value, target coverage 80%. Range = prediction +/- bin half-width, clipped to 0..1. Grid, solar and unserved are bounded separately, so the three ranges do not sum to 1.
coverage_check: Nested spatial coverage: grid 80%, solar 80%, unserved 80%
labels: Kenya DHS 2022 (DHS-8), restricted data. Only model-derived outputs are published.
feature_sources: population: WorldPop/GP/100m/pop (2020) [CC BY 4.0]; built_up_surface: JRC/GHSL/P2023A/GHS_BUILT_S (2020) [CC BY 4.0]; night_lights_bm: NASA/VIIRS/002/VNP46A2 (Black Marble) median 2024-01-01 to 2026-01-01 [NASA open data, cite Black Marble (confirm)]; travel_time_city: projects/malariaatlasproject/assets/accessibility/accessibility_to_cities/2015_v1_0 [CC BY 4.0]; travel_time_health: projects/malariaatlasproject/assets/accessibility/accessibility_to_healthcare/2019 [CC BY 4.0]; slope: USGS/SRTMGL1_003 (ee.Terrain.slope on 100 m mean elevation) [Public domain]; elevation: USGS/SRTMGL1_003 [Public domain]
limitations: Modelled estimate from 1690 survey clusters, not a census. Training label is the MAIN lighting source (DHS hv262), so households using grid plus solar count as grid. DHS cluster locations are displaced by up to 2 km (urban) and 5 km (rural). Solar versus unserved is separated less well than grid versus non-grid. Night lights and satellite layers cannot see small solar systems. Unserved here means no grid and no solar as the main light source (mostly torch and fuel lighting), not the official access gap. National shares from the map are about 8 points lower on grid and 7 higher on unserved than the survey. Mostly this is weighting: the map weights cells by people, the survey weights households, and urban households are smaller; WorldPop also places more people in the remote north-east than the survey sample does. Cell predictions are unbiased where clusters exist. Quote rankings, not national levels. The range is calibrated on cluster-level errors, which include household sampling noise (about 25 households per cluster) and GPS displacement, so it is wider than the uncertainty of the true cell share. Coverage holds on average across districts, not for every cell.
title: Low end of the 80% range for the grid share, 1 km
